title: Commitment and Consistency
hook: Nobody says yes to the big ask first. They say yes to a tiny one, then keep saying yes.
statement: A small first commitment makes people want to stay consistent and say yes to bigger ones later.
explainer: People like acting in line with what they've already done. That's why onboarding that gets users to set a goal or customize something early keeps way more of them around.
sop: Name the big commitment you ultimately want.
Design a tiny first step that points toward it.
Make that step visible, like a profile or a public post.
Build the next step on top of it.
Don't ask for too much too early.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Initial Step 8, Visibility 6, Time 5. (8 + 6 + 5) ÷ 3 = 6.3. Higher means customers are primed for your next, bigger ask. Lower means the first step didn't build enough momentum to carry forward.
question: Write down the smallest first yes you could ask a new customer for.
closing_statement: A small yes today shapes a bigger yes tomorrow.
caption:
Principle Nº 300: Commitment and Consistency

Nobody says yes to the big ask first. They say yes to a tiny one, then keep saying yes.

A small first commitment makes people want to stay consistent and say yes to bigger ones later.
